name: No Signal, No Mercy
creator: Anonymous; attributed to a rotating collective called 'Dead Channel'
description: Distributed exclusively through stolen BCI broadcast windows — brief, unpredictable intrusions into dormant commercial neural feed channels — No Signal, No Mercy delivers dense, furious political commentary on corponation governance, the tier system, augmentation inequality, and what its hosts call 'the infrastructure of managed despair.' Episodes run between eight and twenty-two minutes, end without warning, and are never repeated on the same channel twice. The hosts' voices are algorithmically scrambled to different voices each episode, but their rhetorical style is consistent enough that regular listeners recognize them immediately.
medium: pirate BCI broadcast / stolen commercial neural feed channels
cultural_impact: No Signal, No Mercy is credited with coining several political phrases that have entered Shelf vernacular, including 'managed despair' and 'the chrome ceiling' — a term for the augmentation cost barrier that prevents Tier 1-2 residents from accessing enhancements that would qualify them for higher-tier employment — demonstrating that pirate media can shape political language at a citywide scale.
controversy: Axiom Security's Digital Enforcement Division has publicly designated Dead Channel as a domestic destabilization operation and claimed — without evidence it has shared publicly — that the collective is funded by an unnamed foreign corponation competitor. This claim is widely disbelieved on the Shelf and widely accepted in Tier 4-5 media.
story_hooks: Dead Channel has obtained an unedited internal HelixCorp document that details the deliberate suppression of affordable augmentation options and wants to broadcast it — but the file contains embedded tracking code that will locate any BCI that opens it.

Axiom Security's Digital Enforcement Division has narrowed Dead Channel's broadcast origin to a three-block radius in Shelf District 12 and is preparing a sweep; someone needs to warn the collective without knowing who they are.

A player character hears their own name mentioned in a No Signal, No Mercy episode — cited as a corporate collaborator — and must determine whether Dead Channel has been fed false intelligence, or whether someone in their own network has been talking.
